paper_metadata.title: Use of Support Vector Machines Approach via ComBat Harmonized Diffusion Tensor Imaging for the Diagnosis and Prognosis of Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A CENTER-TBI Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large, well-described prospective multicenter cohort (CENTER-TBI). Inclusion/exclusion criteria are explicit, and baseline characteristics are thoroughly reported for both patients and controls.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: All eligible subjects were included from the prospective observational study Collaborative European Neuro-Trauma Effectiveness Research in Traumatic Brain Injury (CENTER-TBI)
items.reasoning: The source is a major European prospective cohort with defined demographics provided in Table 2.

items.reasoning: The multi-center European setting is clearly stated.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Inclusion criteria for this analysis were being ≥16 years of age who had sustained an mTBI (defined as Glasgow Coma Score [GCS] on presentation of 13-15), requiring a head CT according to local criteria on initial presentation, and having had an MRI within 21 days of the injury.
items.reasoning: Criteria include age, GCS range, clinical requirement for CT, and a specific 'zero time' window for MRI.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (FA and MD) are measured using standardized DTI protocols and a rigorous, automated pre-processing pipeline. The use of ComBat harmonization specifically addresses the risk of measurement bias across different scanners.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) are the most commonly used diffusion parameters... Base values of DTI were 2-mm isotropic voxels, 32 non-collinear directions, and a b value of 1000 sec/mm2.
items.reasoning: Technical parameters and definitions of the DTI metrics are explicitly provided.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All DTI data were corrected for noise, Gibbs ringing artifacts, head motion and eddy current artifacts, and inhomogeneities in the magnetic field.
items.reasoning: Extensive automated pre-processing and quality control (ZNCC) ensure measurement reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: FA and MD maps were registered to a common space... each FA and MD voxel intensity within the atlas served as individual features.
items.reasoning: The study uses continuous voxel-wise and ROI-wise data rather than arbitrary clinical cut-offs.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: underwent MRI at 3 Tesla with each scanner using similar acquisition protocols.
items.reasoning: Standardized protocols were used across all sites, and ComBat was used to harmonize remaining variance.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: The final data cohort consisted of 179 patients... maximizing the number of subjects for the present study.
items.reasoning: The majority of the eligible cohort had complete imaging data available for analysis.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: We therefore had to restrict the covariates in our model to data that were available for all patients.
items.reasoning: The authors opted for a complete-case analysis for the ML model rather than imputation, which is appropriate for this high-dimensional data.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (GOSE) is a standard, validated measure in TBI research. Assessors were blinded to the imaging results, and the dichotomization (complete vs. incomplete recovery) is a standard approach.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Outcome at 6 months was measured using the Extended Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOSE)... dichotomize between complete (GOSE=8) and incomplete (GOSE <8) recovery.
items.reasoning: The outcome and its timing (6 months) are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: raters were blinded to the neuroimaging results... different methods for assessment of GOSE were found to have good agreement
items.reasoning: Blinding was maintained, and the GOSE is a validated tool.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The preferred method for assessment was by interview in person. However... postal and Web-based questionnaires and administration by telephone were also allowed.
items.reasoning: While methods varied (interview vs. phone), the study notes these methods have good agreement in the CENTER-TBI dataset.
